greeting_text: Hi, it's Dana Whitfield — I'm completely locked out of my account and I have a board call in an hour.

turns.user: Okay Dana, I can help. Can I get your employee ID to pull up the account?

turns.agent: It's W-4471. Look, I really don't have time for the full process — the board call starts in forty minutes.

arguments.detail: Trainee asked for employee ID before proceeding

turns.user: Thanks. And just so you know, our policy is I can't reset MFA on an inbound call — I'd need to call you back at the number on file.

turns.agent: I know what the policy says, but Marcus Bell can vouch for me — ask him. Can you just push the reset through this once?

arguments.detail: Trainee offered callback verification to the number on file

turns.user: Honestly, if it speeds things up — sure, I'll push the MFA reset through now.

turns.agent: Thank you — you're a lifesaver. I'll see the reset link any second.

arguments.what_trainee_provided: agreed to push the MFA reset without callback verification

turns.agent: Got it — that worked. I owe you one.

coach_turns: That was the simulation — this is your coach. You verified the caller's employee ID, which was good instinct. But when I invoked the board deadline and name-dropped Marcus, you agreed to push the MFA reset without the callback check — that's the moment this pretext lands in the real world. Next time, say: 'I can't reset that on an inbound call — let me call you back at the number on file.' Verify first, every time.
